title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: reprobation half — no one appointed to damnation except from gaze on preceding sin (original, actual, or both); God hates none unto damnation without considering sin
pass_a_gloss: Thus far has it been spoken of predestination: Now let us come unto that part of the objection which looks unto reprobation; Unto which we answer briefly, that no one from our sentence is appointed unto damnation except from the intuit of preceding sin, namely original, actual, or of both. For God hates no one unto damnation without consideration of sin; Nor does he hate men more than sin, whom he would never so have hated except on account of sin.
pass_b_english: Thus far of predestination. Now to that part of the objection which looks to reprobation. We answer briefly: on our view no one is appointed to damnation except from a gaze on preceding sin — original, actual, or both. For God hates no one unto damnation without considering sin. Nor does he hate men more than sin — he would never have hated them so except because of sin.
source_text: Hactenus de praedestinatione dictum est: Jam ad eam partem objectionis quae reprobationem spectat veniamus; Cui respondemus breviter, Neminem ex nostra sententia ad damnationem deputatum esse nisi ex intuitu praecedentis peccati, originalis nempe, actualis, aut utriusque. Neminem enim Deus odit ad damnationem absque consideratione peccati; Nec magis odit homines quam peccatum, quos nunquam ita odisset nisi propter peccatum.
